In the simulation, that becomes the variant’s hidden appeal plus noise. an LLMReads the fact sheet and the current lessons, and writes new subject and body variants as JSON.

div.div:
2 · Checks
fixed rules, not a modelEvery variant is checked against the fact sheet:
• no number or price that isn't on it
• no banned phrase
• no misleading “Re:” or “Fwd:”
• subject within the length limit
A rejected variant is rewritten, never sent.
Planned (#13)

div.div:
3 · Judge
a System 1 decision modelRates each variant’s appeal to each segment, once: a calibrated score from 1 to 10. In the simulation, that becomes the variant’s hidden appeal plus noise. It stands in for merchants, and is a different kind of model from the writer.
Today: each variant’s hidden quality is a placeholder setting
Planned (#13): TypeSafe Jev 1.14, via OpenRouter’s Decisions API

div.div:
4 · Scorer
statistics, not an LLMThompson sampling picks what each merchant gets:
• subject and body (tested in Idle)
• timing: +1 hour, +2 days or +5 days
• offer, for Trialists: none, 7 more trial days or 50% off
• the 8% holdout gets no email (ghost sends only)
Today: works in the simulation
